title: How to Use the Google Chat API and Pick Your Auth
summary: Google Chat API is a REST interface for building chat apps and managing spaces, messages, and members. Enable it and send requests at no per-request cost.
body_markdown:
## Stage 3: Send a first message with messages.create


Whose name appears on a first message depends on the token you send; the message itself is one authenticated POST to the space's messages endpoint with a text body.


That's the ownership question again: when this call fails at 2am, the sender identity tells you whose credential to check.


Read the sequence below as the whole call from start to finish. Take from it that only the token step differs between app and user authentication; the rest is identical.


1. Find the space ID from the space URL or from` spaces.list` .
2. Get a bearer token for the identity you chose.
3. POST to` /v1/spaces/SPACE_ID/messages` with` {"text": "..."}` .
4. Read the` name` field in the response.


Each step is expanded below.


### Find the space ID


Open the space in Chat and look at the URL. The identifier after the room segment is the space ID.


If you can't reach the space in a browser, call` spaces.list` and take the ID from each result's` name` , which reads` spaces/` followed by the ID.


An app only lists spaces it belongs to, so a missing space usually means the app was never added to it.


### Make the call


Send the token in an` Authorization: Bearer` header, set the content type to JSON, and put the text in the body. With curl that's a single request to` https://chat.googleapis.com/v1/spaces/SPACE_ID/messages` .


The Google API client libraries wrap the same operation as` spaces.messages.create` , and they handle token refresh for you. That matters more once the script runs unattended.


Check that the token carries a message-creating scope. A token without one is rejected, and the error names the scope problem rather than the space.


If you only need to post into one space and never read anything back, an incoming webhook is a lighter alternative. You create it in the space settings and post to its URL with no OAuth flow.


The cost is that it posts as a webhook, so it can't reach other spaces or call any other method. Choose it knowingly.


### Read the messages.create response from the Chat API


When the call succeeds, it returns the created message. Its` name` field has the form` spaces/SPACE_ID/messages/MESSAGE_ID` , and that string is the handle for every later operation on the message: updating it, deleting it, or replying in a thread.


Store it wherever your automation logs its actions, so the person on call can trace a post back to the run that made it.


Then open the space. The text should be there, attributed to the app or the user, depending on the token. If the message is missing, the response and the sender are the first two things to check.
